hints: Start by drawing pentan-3-ol and notice its symmetry, with two identical ethyl groups on the carbon bearing the OH.
Think about which reaction creates a C=C double bond from this alcohol, since alkenes can show E/Z stereoisomerism.
Recall that pent-2-ene can exist as two different geometric forms around the double bond, so look for the dehydrating reagent.
walkthrough:
**Draw the starting alcohol**

Look closely at pentan-3-ol, it is a symmetrical secondary alcohol.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CH}_3$$
The carbon with the OH is bonded to H, OH, and two identical $\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$ groups. This symmetry is the key to the whole question.

**Check what each reagent does**

Remember the four classic reactions of alcohols. Oxidation gives a ketone, concentrated sulfuric acid causes elimination to an alkene, carboxylic acid gives an ester, and HCl gives a chloroalkane.

**Test each product for stereoisomerism**

Oxidation gives pentan-3-one, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_3$, with no chiral centre and no C=C bond. Esterification gives $\text{CH}_3\text{COOCH(CH}_2\text{CH}_3)_2$ and substitution gives $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHClCH}_2\text{CH}_3$, both still have two identical ethyl groups so they are achiral and have no stereoisomers.

**Spot the alkene that can show E/Z isomerism**

Dehydration (elimination of water) gives mainly pent-2-ene:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CH}_3 \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH=CHCH}_2\text{CH}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$
Pent-2-ene has different groups on each end of the C=C bond, so it exists as E (trans) and Z (cis) stereoisomers, giving a mixture.

options.A: Acidified potassium dichromate oxidises the secondary alcohol to pentan-3-one. A ketone has a planar C=O with no chiral centre and no C=C bond, so no stereoisomers are formed.
options.B: Concentrated sulfuric acid dehydrates pentan-3-ol by elimination to give pent-2-ene. Pent-2-ene shows E/Z (cis-trans) stereoisomerism around the C=C double bond, so a mixture of stereoisomers is obtained.
options.C: Ethanoic acid with concentrated H2SO4 gives esterification to 1-ethylpropyl ethanoate, CH3COOCH(CH2CH3)2. The central carbon still has two identical ethyl groups, so the ester is achiral and has no stereoisomers.
options.D: Hydrogen chloride gives nucleophilic substitution to 3-chloropentane, CH3CH2CHClCH2CH3. Like the starting alcohol, C-3 carries two identical ethyl groups, so the molecule is achiral and does not exist as stereoisomers.
